source.title: France or Spain or Germany or France: A Neural Account of Non-Redundant Redundant Disjunctions
source.authors: Sasha Boguraev; Qing Yao; Kyle Mahowald

page_placements.theme: Specialisation and polysemanticity of induction heads; token-specific feature decomposition

record.tranche_reason: The study measures attention from previously identified induction heads in a new repeated-item task, using a different task and measurement from the original induction-head work.
record.gate_note: Experiment 3 measures attention patterns of induction heads in Llama2-7b across critical and control conditions. It does not test induction-head formation during training, loss curves, in-context-learning gains, or causally remove or intervene on the heads. Experiment 1 reports repeated-item completion behavior across models, but does not attribute those behaviors to induction heads. The heads analyzed were identified by prior work.
record.test_reason: The study takes Llama2-7b induction heads already identified by Feucht et al. (2025). It uses their attention patterns to explain a linguistic phenomenon, non-redundant repeated disjuncts. It does not identify or validate induction heads, study their formation or composition with previous-token heads, relate them to in-context-learning loss, or compare across models. Its finding is how known induction heads behave in one new context, which no version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that contextual binding of repeated disjuncts, shown causally by activation patching, combines with selective attention by induction heads to explain LM repeated-item behaviour. The heads' sensitivity to surface order explains the LM ordering effects.
record.recipe_differences: Measures attention patterns of previously identified heads on a new linguistic task; does not reproduce the original training-dynamics or induction-head formation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Attention is strongest when the second disjunction’s surface order matches and is much weaker when it does not; the control condition shows no corresponding pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama2-7b, the top-9 causally important induction heads (from Feucht et al.) attend strongly to the context-licensed repeated item in critical disjunction stimuli. They show no such attention in a list control. Attention is much weaker when the second disjunct's surface order mismatches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-head attention in pretrained LLMs is gated by context and surface order, not applied uniformly to every repeated token.

record.problems: The head analysis is limited to Llama2-7b and relies on heads identified in prior work. Attention is reported in figures without numerical estimates or uncertainty, and the study does not causally intervene on the heads to demonstrate copying.
record.rows_left_out: Experiment 1 reports repeated-item generation behavior across 12 models, but does not measure or attribute that behavior to induction heads; it was therefore not included as a row for these versions. Experiment 2 measures contextual binding rather than induction-head behavior.

untested.parts: No small attention-only models, no previous-token head composition, and no causal test of copying.
Only Llama2-7b, with heads identified by prior work, so no new evidence on cross-family presence.
No variation of training data or training setup.
No comparison between few-shot learning and copying mechanisms.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its V1/V4 'supports' labels are removed. The heads are taken as given from prior work, and the analysis is correlational attention only, in a single model. Experiment 1 shows that pythia-70m repeats the most recent noun, but the study does not attribute this to induction heads.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test formation in small attention-only transformers, composition with an earlier previous-token head, or causal copying in the canonical [A][B] … [A] → [B] pattern.
Tests induction-head attention only in Llama2-7b; does not test other model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.

relation.reason: Head identification and induction-related causal importance come from Feucht et al. (2025); this study measures their attention on linguistic stimuli.

tranche.reason: Uses previously identified induction heads to explain disjunction completion through attention patterns; does not test any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Top-9 causal importance refers to prior sentence-repetition work. This study's activation patching establishes contextual binding; its head-attention analysis does not causally establish copying by those heads.
